newsitem.title: JORDAN: King Hussein of Jordan orders parliament elections.
newsitem.headline: King Hussein of Jordan orders parliament elections.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein on Wednesday formally instructed his government to prepare for elections later this year, the official Petra news agency reported.
Citing Jordan's constitution which gives the monarch responsibility for calling the elections, King Hussein ordered "that the elections for the council of deputies be held according to the law".
He did not set a date for the elections, due to be held within four years of last elections in November 1993.
The standard parliamentary term in Jordan is four years but according to the constitution King Hussein could have decided to extend the existing parliament if he wished.
Political analysts said the cabinet of Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali was likely to set a date for the elections at a regular ministerial meeting on Saturday.

The influential Moslem Brotherhood has already called for a boycott of the polls, complaining that parliament has been sidelined in the four years since the last elections. Most opposition parties have yet to decide whether they will put up candidates.
